note: Re-judged after the R3 split: the row is now only the Section 1 clause 'MUST be configurable via management interfaces' (the IKE negotiation clause is the gap row RFC4303-1-2). Forbidden behaviour: the management interface refusing, or silently altering, an integrity-only ESP configuration. Positive: TestIPsecESPRequiresIntegrity drives esp + null cipher + sha256 through parseOSPFConfig/validateConfig and t.Fatalf on any refusal. Negative (R1(b), inputs pushed toward a refusal): TestRFC4303IntegrityOnlyESPIsConfigurable, for every integrity algorithm in ipsecAuthKeyLen x {cipher leaf omitted, explicit null}, validates and installs and asserts proto 50 (not AH), cipher null with no key, and the configured integrity algorithm and key length, so a validator requiring a cipher for ESP or accepting integrity-only for one algorithm only goes red. The old negative (null cipher with no integrity refused) proved RFC4303-3.2-1 and was removed from this row. Revert records on validateESPConfidentiality for both units observed red (positive recorded by this judge). Only the OSPFv3 manual-SA surface offers integrity-only ESP; IKE's absence is RFC4303-1-2.
